In [[invariant theory]], a branch of algebra, given a group ''G'', a '''covariant''' is a ''G''-[[equivariant]] [[polynomial map]] <math>V \to W</math> between [[linear representation]]s ''V'', ''W'' of ''G''.<ref>{{harvnb|Kraft|Procesi|2016|loc=§ 1.4.}}</ref> It is a generalization of a classical convariant,{{clarify|reason=covariant or coinvariant?|date=February 2020}} which is a homogeneous [[polynomial map]] from the space of binary ''m''-forms to the space of binary ''p''-forms (over the complex numbers) that is [[equivariant map|<math>SL_2(\mathbb{C})</math>-equivariant]].<ref>{{harvnb|Procesi|2007|loc=Ch 15. § 1.1.}}</ref>
